stories.headline: Lockheed Martin to establish HIMARS maintenance center in Estonia
stories.summary: US defense contractor Lockheed Martin will build a HIMARS missile system maintenance facility in Estonia to serve all three Baltic states. The agreement was reached during Defense Minister Pevkur's visit to Washington and represents a $10 million investment over two years.

stories.headline: Russian Su-30 fighter jet violates Estonian airspace
stories.summary: A Russian Su-30 fighter aircraft spent about one minute in Estonian airspace on March 18. Foreign Minister Tsahkna confirmed the violation, noting it was the first Russian airspace breach of 2026 and that 'the season has begun,' though there was no direct threat to Estonian security.

stories.headline: Explosion at Russian military base near Estonian border
stories.summary: A large explosion occurred at a Russian military base in Pskov, 32 kilometers from Estonia. Defense Minister Pevkur stated it was likely a fuel depot that was hit, possibly by Ukrainian forces, though details remained unclear pending further verification.

stories.headline: Estonian Foreign Minister visits Israel in solidarity amid Iran war
stories.summary: Foreign Minister Tsahkna conducted an official visit to Israel, meeting with counterpart Gideon Sa'ar to express Estonia's firm support for Israel during the ongoing conflict with Iran. Tsahkna emphasized shared values of freedom and declared that the Iran war affects Estonia too.

stories.headline: EU adopts Estonia's proposal to restrict visas for Russian fighters
stories.summary: The European Union has taken up Estonia's proposal to restrict visa access for Russian military personnel who fought in Ukraine. Foreign Minister Tsahkna first raised the issue in January, arguing that Russian fighters pose security threats to Europe and could be recruited by Russian intelligence.
